question_text: Was the Mitsui Shopping Park app hacked?
answer_text: Yes, by the companies' own account. Mitsui Fudosan and its shopping-centre arm say a third party got into the app without authorisation, and data on about 3.1 million point-card members leaked.
label: Confirmed

question_text: What data leaked in the Mitsui Shopping Park app breach?
answer_text: Member number, name, date of birth, address, email address, phone number and gender, for about 3,119,000 members, the companies say. Credit card details and passwords were not included.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Have payments or points been misused after the breach?
answer_text: The companies say they have found no misuse of app payments or points and no fraudulent orders so far. That is their word; nobody outside has checked it. They warn members to watch for fake emails.
label: Reported

question_text: How did the intruder get into the Mitsui Shopping Park app, and who was it?
what_would_settle_it: The companies or investigators saying how the intruder got in and who was behind it.

question_text: When will the Mitsui Shopping Park app be back?
answer_text: It is back. The companies said on Nov 27 that the app had restarted, once it was ready to be used safely. Some members who pay through the app may need to register their card again.
label: Confirmed
what_would_settle_it: The companies announcing that the app has restarted, by email, in the app, on LINE or on the shopping centres' sites, as they say they will.
